heading: Block shape
text:
### Block shape [LTSL.2.3]

A test block is a name and a set of sections (`test_decl`, [LGRA.21.1]):
`initial`, the starting state; `inputs`, the input timeline; `responses`, the
replies to outbound calls; and `produces`, the expected outputs.

A test block must contain a `produces` section; `initial`, `inputs`, and
`responses` are optional, and an optional top-level `until <dur>` ([LTSL.3.5]) may
also appear. A section keyword must not appear more than once per test. A test with
no `inputs` asserts only over time passage and must supply `until` to advance the
clock.

The compiler must refuse each violation, with its own code: a test with no
`produces` section with `DS_VALIDATE_TEST_NO_PRODUCES`; a section keyword
repeated within one test with `DS_VALIDATE_TEST_DUPLICATE_SECTION`; and a test
with neither `inputs` nor `until` with `DS_VALIDATE_TEST_NO_INPUTS_OR_UNTIL`. A
repeated section is refused, not merged or overridden.
